```{r}
country_name <- "United States"

# filter out na and sort by year
df_cleaned_owid <- owid_kaya_data %>%
  filter(Entity == country_name) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(population), 
    !is.na(gdp_percap), 
    !is.na(energy_intensity), 
    !is.na(carbon_intensity_co2_energy),
    !is.na(co2_emissions)
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year)

print(paste("Number of complete years available for analysis:", nrow(df_cleaned_owid)))
head(df_cleaned_owid)

# available years check
df_cleaned_owid %>% 
  summarise(
    first_year = min(Year), 
    last_year = max(Year)
  )

# select desired years
df_target_range <- df_cleaned_owid %>%
  filter(Year >= 1994 & Year <= max(Year))


print(paste("Number of continuous years in the analysis range:", nrow(df_target_range)))
print(paste("Years range from", min(df_target_range$Year), "to", max(df_target_range$Year)))
```

```{r}
# mutate variables to standard kaya
df_kaya_factors <- df_target_range %>%
  mutate(
    p = population,                                
    g = gdp_percap,                                
    i = energy_intensity,                          
    f = carbon_intensity_co2_energy,               
    
    # Raw identity product in t
    kaya_product = (p * g * i * f) / 1000000,
    
    # Discrepancy residual for every individual year
    r = co2_emissions / kaya_product
  ) %>%
  select(Entity, Year, co2_emissions, p, g, i, f, r)

# Preview the factor timeline
head(df_kaya_factors, 10)
```

```{r}
df_lmdi_pct <- df_kaya_factors %>%
  mutate(
    # 1. Create lagged columns to line up year t-1 next to year t
    co2_t1     = lag(co2_emissions),
    p_t1       = lag(p),
    g_t1       = lag(g),
    i_t1       = lag(i),
    f_t1       = lag(f),
    r_t1       = lag(r),
    year_start = lag(Year),
    year_end   = Year
  ) %>%
  # Drop the very first row (1994) since it has no baseline year
  filter(!is.na(co2_t1)) %>%
  
  # 2. Compute absolute LMDI effects first
  mutate(
    delta_co2 = co2_emissions - co2_t1,
    w_t = if_else(delta_co2 == 0, co2_emissions, delta_co2 / (log(co2_emissions) - log(co2_t1))),
    
    effect_population        = w_t * log(p / p_t1),
    effect_affluence         = w_t * log(g / g_t1),
    effect_energy_intensity  = w_t * log(i / i_t1),
    effect_carbon_intensity  = w_t * log(f / f_t1),
    effect_residual          = w_t * log(r / r_t1)
  ) %>%
  
  # 3. Convert absolute effects into percentage contributions relative to base year emissions (co2_t1)
  mutate(
    # Total actual % change of emissions
    pct_change_co2              = (delta_co2 / co2_t1) * 100,
    
    # % contribution of each individual driver
    pct_effect_population       = (effect_population / co2_t1) * 100,
    pct_effect_affluence        = (effect_affluence / co2_t1) * 100,
    pct_effect_energy_intensity = (effect_energy_intensity / co2_t1) * 100,
    pct_effect_carbon_intensity = (effect_carbon_intensity / co2_t1) * 100,
    pct_effect_residual         = (effect_residual / co2_t1) * 100,
    
    # Verification sum (should equal pct_change_co2 exactly)
    sum_pct_effects = pct_effect_population + pct_effect_affluence + pct_effect_energy_intensity + 
      pct_effect_carbon_intensity + pct_effect_residual
  ) %>%
  
  # 4. Clean up the table to isolate the percentage metrics
  select(year_start, year_end, pct_change_co2, pct_effect_population, pct_effect_affluence, 
         pct_effect_energy_intensity, pct_effect_carbon_intensity, pct_effect_residual, sum_pct_effects)

# View the percentage decomposition table
head(df_lmdi_pct)
```

```{r}
# 1. Reshape the data from wide to long format for ggplot
df_lmdi_pct_long <- df_lmdi_pct %>%
  select(year_end, pct_effect_population, pct_effect_affluence, 
         pct_effect_energy_intensity, pct_effect_carbon_intensity, pct_effect_residual) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("pct_effect_"), 
    names_to = "socioeconomic_driver", 
    values_to = "percentage_contribution"
  ) %>%
  # 2. Clean up the label names for the chart legend to make them presentable
  mutate(socioeconomic_driver = case_when(
    socioeconomic_driver == "pct_effect_population"       ~ "Population Growth",
    socioeconomic_driver == "pct_effect_affluence"        ~ "Economic Affluence (GDP/Capita)",
    socioeconomic_driver == "pct_effect_energy_intensity" ~ "Energy Intensity (Energy/GDP)",
    socioeconomic_driver == "pct_effect_carbon_intensity" ~ "Carbon Intensity (CO2/Energy)",
    socioeconomic_driver == "pct_effect_residual"         ~ "Data Discrepancy Residual"
  ))

# 3. Create the stacked bar chart for percentage contributions
ggplot(df_lmdi_pct_long, aes(x = year_end, y = percentage_contribution, fill = socioeconomic_driver)) +
  geom_col() + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black", size = 0.5) + 
  labs(
    title = paste("Kaya Identity LMDI Decomposition:", country_name),
    subtitle = "Annual percentage point contributions to total CO₂ emissions change (1994-2022)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Contribution to Emissions Change (Percentage Points)",
    fill = "Kaya Identity Component"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  ) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2")
```

```{r}
#LOOPED CHART MAKER

# 1. Define the vector of countries you want to analyze
country_list <- c("United States", "Germany", "China", "Brazil", "Angola", "Laos", "Czechia")


# 2. Execute the loop across each country in your list
for (current_country in country_list) {
  
  message(paste("Processing Kaya LMDI decomposition for:", current_country))
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # STEP 3: FILTER AND CLEAN DATA FOR THE CURRENT COUNTRY
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  df_cleaned_owid <- owid_kaya_data %>%
    filter(Entity == current_country) %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(population), 
      !is.na(gdp_percap), 
      !is.na(energy_intensity), 
      !is.na(carbon_intensity_co2_energy),
      !is.na(co2_emissions)
    ) %>%
    arrange(Year)
  
  # Extract the continuous range from 1994 onwards
  df_target_range <- df_cleaned_owid %>%
    filter(Year >= 1994 & Year <= max(Year))
  
  # Safety Check: Skip the country if there isn't enough historical data points
  if (nrow(df_target_range) < 2) {
    warning(paste("Not enough continuous data points from 1994 onwards for", current_country, "- skipping."))
    next
  }
  
  # Capture the latest available year dynamically for chart subtitles
  latest_year <- max(df_target_range$Year)
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # STEP 4: DEFINE KAYA FACTORS AND ACCOUNTING RESIDUAL (r)
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  df_kaya_factors <- df_target_range %>%
    mutate(
      p = population,                                
      g = gdp_percap,                                
      i = energy_intensity,                          
      f = carbon_intensity_co2_energy,               
      
      # Raw identity product (scaled to Tonnes)
      kaya_product = (p * g * i * f) / 1000000,
      
      # Discrepancy residual for every individual year
      r = co2_emissions / kaya_product
    ) %>%
    select(Entity, Year, co2_emissions, p, g, i, f, r)
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # STEPS 5 & 7: CALCULATE YEAR-OVER-YEAR LMDI PERCENTAGE EFFECTS
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  df_lmdi_pct <- df_kaya_factors %>%
    mutate(
      co2_t1     = lag(co2_emissions),
      p_t1       = lag(p),
      g_t1       = lag(g),
      i_t1       = lag(i),
      f_t1       = lag(f),
      r_t1       = lag(r),
      year_start = lag(Year),
      year_end   = Year
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(co2_t1)) %>%
    mutate(
      # Absolute change and Logarithmic Weight
      delta_co2 = co2_emissions - co2_t1,
      w_t = if_else(delta_co2 == 0, co2_emissions, delta_co2 / (log(co2_emissions) - log(co2_t1))),
      
      # Absolute effects
      effect_population        = w_t * log(p / p_t1),
      effect_affluence         = w_t * log(g / g_t1),
      effect_energy_intensity  = w_t * log(i / i_t1),
      effect_carbon_intensity  = w_t * log(f / f_t1),
      effect_residual          = w_t * log(r / r_t1),
      
      # Convert absolute effects into baseline-relative percentage points
      pct_effect_population       = (effect_population / co2_t1) * 100,
      pct_effect_affluence        = (effect_affluence / co2_t1) * 100,
      pct_effect_energy_intensity = (effect_energy_intensity / co2_t1) * 100,
      pct_effect_carbon_intensity = (effect_carbon_intensity / co2_t1) * 100,
      pct_effect_residual         = (effect_residual / co2_t1) * 100,
      
      # Actual total net % change of emissions
      pct_change_co2              = (delta_co2 / co2_t1) * 100
    )
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # STEPS 6 & 8: RESHAPE AND VISUALIZE THE RESULTS
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  df_lmdi_pct_long <- df_lmdi_pct %>%
    select(year_end, pct_effect_population, pct_effect_affluence, 
           pct_effect_energy_intensity, pct_effect_carbon_intensity, pct_effect_residual) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = starts_with("pct_effect_"), 
      names_to = "socioeconomic_driver", 
      values_to = "percentage_contribution"
    ) %>%
    mutate(socioeconomic_driver = case_when(
      socioeconomic_driver == "pct_effect_population"       ~ "Population Growth",
      socioeconomic_driver == "pct_effect_affluence"        ~ "Economic Affluence (GDP/Capita)",
      socioeconomic_driver == "pct_effect_energy_intensity" ~ "Energy Intensity (Energy/GDP)",
      socioeconomic_driver == "pct_effect_carbon_intensity" ~ "Carbon Intensity (CO2/Energy)",
      socioeconomic_driver == "pct_effect_residual"         ~ "Data Discrepancy Residual"
    ))
  
  # Construct the percentage chart with an overlaid net-change line
  pct_plot <- ggplot() +
    # 1. Add the stacked columns for individual drivers
    geom_col(
      data = df_lmdi_pct_long, 
      aes(x = year_end, y = percentage_contribution, fill = socioeconomic_driver)
    ) + 
    
    # 2. Overlay the line showing net emissions change
    geom_line(
      data = df_lmdi_pct, 
      aes(x = year_end, y = pct_change_co2, group = 1, color = "Net CO₂ Change"), 
      linewidth = 1
    ) +
    
    # 3. Add points on the line
    geom_point(
      data = df_lmdi_pct, 
      aes(x = year_end, y = pct_change_co2, color = "Net CO₂ Change"), 
      size = 1.8
    ) +
    
    # 4. Styling, axes, and cosmetic layers (COMPACTED LEGEND DESIGN)
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black", size = 0.5) + 
    labs(
      title = paste("Kaya Identity LMDI Decomposition:", current_country),
      subtitle = paste0("Annual percentage point contributions vs. total net CO₂ change (1994-", latest_year, ")"),
      x = "Year",
      y = "Emissions Change (Percentage Points / %)",
      fill = "Kaya Identity Component",
      color = "Total Trend"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.box = "vertical", 
      legend.margin = margin(t = 2, r = 0, b = 2, l = 0, unit = "pt"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 7.5),                 # Shrinks text of legend elements
      legend.title = element_text(size = 8.5, face = "bold"),  # Shrinks font of titles
      legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"),                     # Makes colored boxes smaller
      legend.spacing.y = unit(0.05, "cm"),                    # Shrinks vertical space between rows
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
    ) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Net CO₂ Change" = "#2c3e50")) +
    
    # Wrap elements into 2 clean rows and center titles to prevent horizontal clipping
    guides(
      fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5),
      color = guide_legend(title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5)
    )
  
  # Explicitly print the plot inside the loop execution context
  print(pct_plot)
}
```

```{r}
# 6-in-1 chart maker and outputter

library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

# 1. Define your target list of 6 countries
country_list <- c("Argentina", "Mexico", "Chile", "Peru", "Brazil", "Panama")

# 2. Initialize an empty list to store the generated plots
saved_plots_list <- list()

# 3. Execute the loop to process data and construct individual plots
for (current_country in country_list) {
  
  message(paste("Processing Kaya LMDI decomposition for:", current_country))
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # STEP 3: FILTER AND CLEAN DATA FOR THE CURRENT COUNTRY
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  df_cleaned_owid <- owid_kaya_data %>%
    filter(Entity == current_country) %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(population), 
      !is.na(gdp_percap), 
      !is.na(energy_intensity), 
      !is.na(carbon_intensity_co2_energy),
      !is.na(co2_emissions)
    ) %>%
    arrange(Year)
  
  # Extract the continuous range from 1994 onwards
  df_target_range <- df_cleaned_owid %>%
    filter(Year >= 1994 & Year <= max(Year))
  
  # Safety Check: Skip the country if there isn't enough historical data points
  if (nrow(df_target_range) < 2) {
    warning(paste("Not enough continuous data points from 1994 onwards for", current_country, "- skipping."))
    next
  }
  
  # Capture latest year dynamically for subtitles
  latest_year <- max(df_target_range$Year)
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # STEP 4: DEFINE KAYA FACTORS AND ACCOUNTING RESIDUAL (r)
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  df_kaya_factors <- df_target_range %>%
    mutate(
      p = population,                                
      g = gdp_percap,                                
      i = energy_intensity,                          
      f = carbon_intensity_co2_energy,               
      
      # Raw identity product (scaled to Tonnes)
      kaya_product = (p * g * i * f) / 1000000,
      
      # Discrepancy residual for every individual year
      r = co2_emissions / kaya_product
    ) %>%
    select(Entity, Year, co2_emissions, p, g, i, f, r)
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # STEPS 5 & 7: CALCULATE YEAR-OVER-YEAR LMDI PERCENTAGE EFFECTS
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  df_lmdi_pct <- df_kaya_factors %>%
    mutate(
      co2_t1     = lag(co2_emissions),
      p_t1       = lag(p),
      g_t1       = lag(g),
      i_t1       = lag(i),
      f_t1       = lag(f),
      r_t1       = lag(r),
      year_start = lag(Year),
      year_end   = Year
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(co2_t1)) %>%
    mutate(
      # Absolute change and Logarithmic Weight
      delta_co2 = co2_emissions - co2_t1,
      w_t = if_else(delta_co2 == 0, co2_emissions, delta_co2 / (log(co2_emissions) - log(co2_t1))),
      
      # Absolute effects
      effect_population        = w_t * log(p / p_t1),
      effect_affluence         = w_t * log(g / g_t1),
      effect_energy_intensity  = w_t * log(i / i_t1),
      effect_carbon_intensity  = w_t * log(f / f_t1),
      effect_residual          = w_t * log(r / r_t1),
      
      # Convert absolute effects into baseline-relative percentage points
      pct_effect_population       = (effect_population / co2_t1) * 100,
      pct_effect_affluence        = (effect_affluence / co2_t1) * 100,
      pct_effect_energy_intensity = (effect_energy_intensity / co2_t1) * 100,
      pct_effect_carbon_intensity = (effect_carbon_intensity / co2_t1) * 100,
      pct_effect_residual         = (effect_residual / co2_t1) * 100,
      
      # Actual total net % change of emissions
      pct_change_co2              = (delta_co2 / co2_t1) * 100
    )
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # STEPS 6 & 8: RESHAPE AND VISUALIZE THE RESULTS
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  df_lmdi_pct_long <- df_lmdi_pct %>%
    select(year_end, pct_effect_population, pct_effect_affluence, 
           pct_effect_energy_intensity, pct_effect_carbon_intensity, pct_effect_residual) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = starts_with("pct_effect_"), 
      names_to = "socioeconomic_driver", 
      values_to = "percentage_contribution"
    ) %>%
    mutate(socioeconomic_driver = case_when(
      socioeconomic_driver == "pct_effect_population"       ~ "Population Growth",
      socioeconomic_driver == "pct_effect_affluence"        ~ "Economic Affluence (GDP/Capita)",
      socioeconomic_driver == "pct_effect_energy_intensity" ~ "Energy Intensity (Energy/GDP)",
      socioeconomic_driver == "pct_effect_carbon_intensity" ~ "Carbon Intensity (CO2/Energy)",
      socioeconomic_driver == "pct_effect_residual"         ~ "Data Discrepancy Residual"
    ))
  
  # Construct the individual percentage chart
  pct_plot <- ggplot() +
    geom_col(
      data = df_lmdi_pct_long, 
      aes(x = year_end, y = percentage_contribution, fill = socioeconomic_driver)
    ) + 
    geom_line(
      data = df_lmdi_pct, 
      aes(x = year_end, y = pct_change_co2, group = 1, color = "Net CO₂ Change"), 
      linewidth = 0.7
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = df_lmdi_pct, 
      aes(x = year_end, y = pct_change_co2, color = "Net CO₂ Change"), 
      size = 1.2
    ) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black", size = 0.4) + 
    labs(
      title = current_country, 
      x = "Year",
      y = "Change (Percentage Points / %)",
      fill = "Kaya Identity Component",
      color = "Total Trend"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 7),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 8)
    ) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Net CO₂ Change" = "#2c3e50"))
  
  saved_plots_list[[current_country]] <- pct_plot
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# COMPILE THE FINAL GRID 
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
final_grid_chart <- wrap_plots(saved_plots_list, ncol = 2, nrow = 3) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Comparative Cross-Country Kaya Identity LMDI Decomposition",
    subtitle = "Annual drivers of emissions vs. total absolute net percentage change (1994-2022)",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.5)
    )
  ) &
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
    legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm")
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SAVE TO A4 LANDSCAPE FILE
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Standard A4 size is 29.7 x 21.0 cm. 
# You can change the extension to ".pdf" if you prefer vector graphic format!
ggsave(
  filename = "kaya_lmdi_decomposition_grid.png", 
  plot = final_grid_chart, 
  width = 29.7, 
  height = 21.0, 
  units = "cm", 
  dpi = 300
)

message("Success! The layout has been saved to your workspace files as 'kaya_lmdi_decomposition_grid.png'.")
```

```{r}
# individual country outputter

library(tidyverse)

# 1. Define the vector of countries you want to analyze
country_list <- c("United States", "Germany", "China", "Brazil", "India", "Laos", "Czechia", "Japan", "South Korea", "Angola", "Kenya")


# 2. Execute the loop across each country in your list
for (current_country in country_list) {
  
  message(paste("Processing Kaya LMDI decomposition for:", current_country))
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # STEP 3: FILTER AND CLEAN DATA FOR THE CURRENT COUNTRY
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  df_cleaned_owid <- owid_kaya_data %>%
    filter(Entity == current_country) %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(population), 
      !is.na(gdp_percap), 
      !is.na(energy_intensity), 
      !is.na(carbon_intensity_co2_energy),
      !is.na(co2_emissions)
    ) %>%
    arrange(Year)
  
  # Extract the continuous range from 1994 onwards
  df_target_range <- df_cleaned_owid %>%
    filter(Year >= 1994 & Year <= max(Year))
  
  # Safety Check: Skip the country if there isn't enough historical data points
  if (nrow(df_target_range) < 2) {
    warning(paste("Not enough continuous data points from 1994 onwards for", current_country, "- skipping."))
    next
  }
  
  # Capture latest year dynamically for chart subtitles
  latest_year <- max(df_target_range$Year)
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # STEP 4: DEFINE KAYA FACTORS AND ACCOUNTING RESIDUAL (r)
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  df_kaya_factors <- df_target_range %>%
    mutate(
      p = population,                                
      g = gdp_percap,                                
      i = energy_intensity,                          
      f = carbon_intensity_co2_energy,               
      
      # Raw identity product (scaled to Tonnes)
      kaya_product = (p * g * i * f) / 1000000,
      
      # Discrepancy residual for every individual year
      r = co2_emissions / kaya_product
    ) %>%
    select(Entity, Year, co2_emissions, p, g, i, f, r)
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # STEPS 5 & 7: CALCULATE YEAR-OVER-YEAR LMDI PERCENTAGE EFFECTS
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  df_lmdi_pct <- df_kaya_factors %>%
    mutate(
      co2_t1     = lag(co2_emissions),
      p_t1       = lag(p),
      g_t1       = lag(g),
      i_t1       = lag(i),
      f_t1       = lag(f),
      r_t1       = lag(r),
      year_start = lag(Year),
      year_end   = Year
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(co2_t1)) %>%
    mutate(
      # Absolute change and Logarithmic Weight
      delta_co2 = co2_emissions - co2_t1,
      w_t = if_else(delta_co2 == 0, co2_emissions, delta_co2 / (log(co2_emissions) - log(co2_t1))),
      
      # Absolute effects
      effect_population        = w_t * log(p / p_t1),
      effect_affluence         = w_t * log(g / g_t1),
      effect_energy_intensity  = w_t * log(i / i_t1),
      effect_carbon_intensity  = w_t * log(f / f_t1),
      effect_residual          = w_t * log(r / r_t1),
      
      # Convert absolute effects into baseline-relative percentage points
      pct_effect_population       = (effect_population / co2_t1) * 100,
      pct_effect_affluence        = (effect_affluence / co2_t1) * 100,
      pct_effect_energy_intensity = (effect_energy_intensity / co2_t1) * 100,
      pct_effect_carbon_intensity = (effect_carbon_intensity / co2_t1) * 100,
      pct_effect_residual         = (effect_residual / co2_t1) * 100,
      
      # Actual total net % change of emissions
      pct_change_co2              = (delta_co2 / co2_t1) * 100
    )
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # STEPS 6 & 8: RESHAPE AND VISUALIZE THE RESULTS
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  df_lmdi_pct_long <- df_lmdi_pct %>%
    select(year_end, pct_effect_population, pct_effect_affluence, 
           pct_effect_energy_intensity, pct_effect_carbon_intensity, pct_effect_residual) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = starts_with("pct_effect_"), 
      names_to = "socioeconomic_driver", 
      values_to = "percentage_contribution"
    ) %>%
    mutate(socioeconomic_driver = case_when(
      socioeconomic_driver == "pct_effect_population"       ~ "Population Growth",
      socioeconomic_driver == "pct_effect_affluence"        ~ "Economic Affluence (GDP/Capita)",
      socioeconomic_driver == "pct_effect_energy_intensity" ~ "Energy Intensity (Energy/GDP)",
      socioeconomic_driver == "pct_effect_carbon_intensity" ~ "Carbon Intensity (CO2/Energy)",
      socioeconomic_driver == "pct_effect_residual"         ~ "Data Discrepancy Residual"
    ))
  
  # Construct the individual percentage chart with overlaid net line
  pct_plot <- ggplot() +
    geom_col(
      data = df_lmdi_pct_long, 
      aes(x = year_end, y = percentage_contribution, fill = socioeconomic_driver)
    ) + 
    geom_line(
      data = df_lmdi_pct, 
      aes(x = year_end, y = pct_change_co2, group = 1, color = "Net CO₂ Change"), 
      linewidth = 1
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = df_lmdi_pct, 
      aes(x = year_end, y = pct_change_co2, color = "Net CO₂ Change"), 
      size = 1.8
    ) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black", size = 0.5) + 
    labs(
      title = paste("Kaya Identity LMDI Decomposition:", current_country),
      subtitle = paste0("Annual percentage point contributions vs. total net CO₂ change (1994-", latest_year, ")"),
      x = "Year",
      y = "Emissions Change (Percentage Points / %)",
      fill = "Kaya Identity Component",
      color = "Total Trend"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.box = "vertical", 
      legend.margin = margin(t = 2, r = 0, b = 2, l = 0, unit = "pt"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 7.5),                 
      legend.title = element_text(size = 8.5, face = "bold"),  
      legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"),                     
      legend.spacing.y = unit(0.05, "cm"),                    
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
    ) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Net CO₂ Change" = "#2c3e50")) +
    guides(
      fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5),
      color = guide_legend(title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5)
    )
  
  # (Optional) Keep printing them in your RStudio interface as they compile
  print(pct_plot)
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # DYNAMIC GGSAVE IMPLEMENTATION WITH SNAKE_CASE FILENAMES
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Converts "United States" into "united_states" to build a clean filename string
  clean_filename_string <- tolower(str_replace_all(current_country, " ", "_"))
  output_filename <- paste0("kaya_lmdi_", clean_filename_string, ".png")
  
  ggsave(
    filename = output_filename,
    plot = pct_plot,
    width = 22.0,
    height = 14.0,
    units = "cm",
    dpi = 300
  )
  
  message(paste("Saved file to workspace as:", output_filename))
}

message("All individual country files successfully saved!")
```
